name: Fermi-LAT
summary: Fermi's main high-energy gamma-ray instrument searches the Galactic center, dwarf spheroidal galaxies, dark subhalos and diffuse sky for indirect dark-matter signals, and also measures cosmic-ray electrons.
detection_principle: Incoming gamma rays convert to electron–positron pairs in tungsten layers. A silicon-strip tracker measures direction, a CsI calorimeter measures energy, and an anticoincidence system rejects charged particles.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: FSSC's operational history records completion of the 100000th orbit on 2026-07-13; the 2019 data-management document is used only as historical mission information.

timeline.event: Commissioning completed; first observing cycle began

results.summary: Established indirect searches across multiple classes of dark-matter-rich targets. This dossier does not interpret the Galactic-center excess as confirmed dark matter.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
